Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
arbusto
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin arbustum, from arbor (“tree”) -tum (“adjective-forming suffix”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /arˈbusto/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -usto
  • Syllabification: ar‧bus‧to

Noun

[edit]

arbusto (accusative singular arbuston, plural arbustoj, accusative plural arbustojn)

  1. shrub, bush, shrubbery

Derived terms

[edit]
  • arbusteto
  • subarbusto
  • trunkarbusto
  • tufarbusto
  • vezikarbusto

Further reading

[edit]
  • “arbusto”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “arbusto”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin arbustum.

Noun

[edit]

arbusto m (plural arbustos)

  1. shrub, bush
    Synonyms: gamallo, garamallo, albustre

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French arbuste, Italian arbusto, Spanish arbusto.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /arˈbusto/

Noun

[edit]

arbusto (plural arbusti)

  1. shrub, bush (not over three feet in height)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • arbustaro (“thicket”)
  • subarbusto (“underbush”)

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From arbustus (“planted with trees”) or arbustum (“orchard”) +‎ -ō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [arˈbʊs.toː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [arˈbus.to]

Verb

[edit]

arbustō (present infinitive arbustāre, perfect active arbustāvī, supine arbustātum); first conjugation

  1. (hapax legomenon) to plant with trees
    • 77 CE – 79 CE, Plinius Maior, Naturalis Historia 17.201:
      Transpādana Italia praeter suprā dictās cornū, opulō, tiliā, acere, ornō, carpinō, quercū arbustat agrōs, Venetia salice propter ūlīginem solī.
      Transpadanian Italy plants the fields with cornel, maple [of some other kind than acer], linden, maple, hornbeam and oak, besides those mentioned above, Veneto with willow on account of the moisture of the soil.
